title: Choosing deterministic automation, predictive AI, generative AI, or an agent
objectives: Choose among deterministic automation, predictive AI, generative AI, and an Agentforce agent using Salesforce Help definitions.
Defend Flow, formula, or validation when the rule must be the same every time.
Send historical scores to predictive AI and drafts to Prompt Builder without standing up an agent by default.
Refuse an agent when grounding, testing, or human approval cannot be named; mark SKUs Needs verification.
diagnostic_question: Four requests arrive: raise Amount by 10 percent on save, score churn from history, draft a renewal email, and chat 24/7 about shipping with escalation. Before reading, which is deterministic automation, predictive AI, generative AI, or an agent?
definition: Choosing the tool starts from the outcome. Deterministic automation—formulas, validation rules, approval processes, and Flow—runs the same configured logic every time. Predictive AI uses machine-learning models and historical data to predict outcomes. Generative AI drafts content from prompt templates. An Agentforce agent converses, selects jobs, and can complete a sequence of tasks on a channel. ([Which Tool to Use](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.process_which_tool.htm); [Predictive AI](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.c360_a_ai_predictive.htm); [Prompt Builder](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_about.htm); [Design and Implement Agents](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_intro.htm))
why_it_matters: The expensive interview fail is an agent for a formula. The other fail is a Flow when the user actually needs a conversation plus actions. Help still publishes a which-tool guide for declarative automation; Einstein and Agentforce did not delete it.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a hospital triage desk. Deterministic automation is the published protocol: this dose, every time. Predictive AI is the risk score from past charts. Generative AI is drafting the discharge summary the clinician still signs. An Agentforce agent is the intern who can talk to the family, look up the chart, and page a human for anything sensitive. You do not ask the intern to calculate 10 percent of Amount, and you do not write a Flow to hold a WhatsApp conversation.
deeper_explanation: Which Tool to Use Help still steers admins among formula fields, validation rules, Flow, and related declarative tools, and it points to approval processes as the tool for formal approvals. Apex remains the complementary tool when declarative paths cannot meet the need. That guide is the deterministic baseline this lesson does not replace. ([Which Tool to Use](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.process_which_tool.htm); [Validation Rules](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.fields_defining_field_validation_rules.htm); [Approval Processes](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_creating_approval_processes.htm))

Predictive AI Help: models built with machine learning and historical data predict business outcomes and recommend ways to improve them. That is a score or forecast written back to records, not a drafted paragraph and not a chat. ([Predictive AI](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.c360_a_ai_predictive.htm))

Prompt Builder Help: reusable prompt templates for generative drafts—Sales Email, Field Generation, Flex—connecting CRM data to LLMs. Use that when a human or an invocable needs generated text, not when the math is fixed. ([Prompt Builder](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_about.htm))

Agentforce Help: the agent-driven layer for AI agents that work beside employees and can serve customers around the clock. Choose an agent when natural language plus a sequence of jobs plus a channel is the requirement, with grounding, Trust, testing, and human transfer from AI-004 through AI-006. ([Design and Implement Agents](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_intro.htm); [Get to Know Agentforce Service Agent](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.bots_service_asa_about.htm))

Combinations are legal: a Flow can call a prompt template; an agent action can launch a Flow; a predictive score can sit on the record the agent reads. Combinations are not a license to skip the first question: what must be the same every time? SKUs remain Needs verification.

mental_model.analogy: A hospital triage desk: protocol, risk score, drafted summary, and an intern who can talk and page a human.
useful_mapping: deterministic automation → published protocol that must not vary
formula / validation / Flow / approval → specific protocol tools
predictive AI → risk score from historical charts
generative AI / Prompt Builder → discharge summary draft
Agentforce agent → intern who converses and completes jobs
Apex → specialist procedure when protocols cannot
where_it_breaks: A hospital has legal clinicians; Salesforce tools have licenses and governors.
An intern is not ASA; do not anthropomorphize liability.
Which Tool to Use does not itself rank Agentforce; this lesson composes that guide with AI Help.
The analogy does not encode Einstein Requests or Data 360 credits.

teach_back_prompt: Without defaulting to an agent, choose a tool for a 10 percent Amount update, a churn score, a renewal email, and a 24/7 shipping chat, then say where the hospital analogy breaks.

review_schedule.prompt: From memory: deterministic vs predictive vs generative vs agent, plus one example each.
Given four stakeholder quotes, choose the tool and the rejected alternative.
When may Flow call a prompt template without becoming an agent?
Refuse an agent that has no grounding or human path.
Two-minute interview: the four-way choose with Help names.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: If it must be the same every time, I use deterministic automation. If it is a score from history, predictive AI. If it is a draft, Prompt Builder. If it is a conversation plus jobs on a channel, an Agentforce agent. I do not start with an agent.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I interview the outcome. Ten percent of Amount is Flow or a formula—Which Tool to Use still applies. Churn from history is predictive AI, not an LLM guess. Renewal email is generative. Shipping chat with escalation is an agent, with grounding, Trust, tests, and a human path. Combinations are fine: Flow can invoke a template; an agent can launch Flow. I refuse an agent with no pantry and no attending. SKUs Needs verification. Copilot is a former name.

interview_questions.question: How do you choose among deterministic automation, predictive AI, generative AI, and an agent?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Same-every-time rules go to Flow, formula, validation, or approvals. Historical scores go to predictive AI. Drafts go to Prompt Builder. Conversation plus jobs on a channel go to Agentforce. I do not start with an agent.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I write four outcome sentences. Which Tool to Use still owns deterministic choice, including when Apex is the complement. Predictive AI Help is ML on history. Prompt Builder is templates. Agentforce is the agent layer, with ASA as the service example. I mention Copilot only as a former name. Combinations are allowed; mega-tools are not. SKUs Needs verification.
interview_questions.example: Discount Flow; churn score; Sales Email; ASA on Enhanced Chat.
tradeoffs: One platform story vs four accurate tools
follow_ups: When is Apex the deterministic complement?

interview_questions.question: Why not a validation rule—or why not an agent—for required Amount on Closed Won?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Requiredness on save is deterministic validation or Flow. An agent will not reliably block the save path and should not be the requiredness engine.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Interviewers love this pairing. Validation rules fire in the save order. Agents converse on channels. If they also want a chat that explains why Amount is required, that is a second outcome: maybe a prompt or an agent FAQ, not a replacement for the rule. I will not delete the validation rule because we bought Agentforce.
interview_questions.example: Validation: Amount required when Stage is Closed Won. Optional FAQ article for sellers.
tradeoffs: One object save vs a channel
weak_answer_warnings: Let the agent remind them instead of a rule

interview_questions.question: A VP wants Agentforce to replace Flow. Your answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I refuse the replacement. Flow remains the deterministic workhorse. Agents may invoke Flow as an action. They do not delete Which Tool to Use.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I show a Venn: same-record updates, approvals, and scheduled jobs stay declarative or Apex. Agents sit on the conversation edge and call those tools. If we try to make the intern calculate every protocol, amounts drift and audits fail. I offer a combination architecture, not a rip-and-replace.
interview_questions.example: Agent action launches LAB_Create_Case Flow; Stage still stamped by before-save Flow.
tradeoffs: Fewer tools vs the right tools
follow_ups: When would Apex still win over Flow?
Can an agent start a Flow interview?

interview_questions.question: Score churn, draft an email, and chat FAQs. How many products?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Three families: predictive AI, Prompt Builder, and an Agentforce agent. Maybe four if discount math is also in the epic. Not one agent.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I draw three boxes with Help URLs. The score is a field. The email is a Sales Email template the rep sends. The FAQ is ASA with a Data Library and transfer. If they insist on one license conversation, I still will not collapse the architecture. SKUs Needs verification.
tradeoffs: One vendor meeting vs three designs
follow_ups: Could the agent read the score?
Could Flow send the email after generation?

interview_questions.question: Where does Apex sit in this four-way choose?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Apex is still the complementary deterministic tool when Flow cannot meet the need. It is not a fourth AI family and not a substitute for an agent channel.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Which Tool to Use and this handbook's AUTO-001 still apply. I write Apex for transaction control, complex branching, or reusable services other Apex must call. I do not write Apex to mimic an LLM, and I do not stand up an agent to avoid a 20-line class that should exist. Agent actions may call Apex; that is combination.
interview_questions.example: LAB_DiscountService for a packaged calculation; ASA still handles FAQ chat.
weak_answer_warnings: Apex is dead because of Agentforce

interview_questions.question: The 'AI discount' fluctuates for the same Opportunity. Diagnose the choose error.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Someone used generative or an agent to do arithmetic. Move it to a formula or Flow. Keep AI for language or conversation if those outcomes remain.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I reproduce two saves with identical inputs. If Amount * 0.9 is not stable, it was never deterministic. I check whether a Field Generation or agent action writes the discount field. I replace it with before-save Flow, add a test, and I tell the stakeholder why LLMs are the wrong calculator. That is this lesson's entire point.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Discounted_Amount__c rewritten by Flow; agent no longer allowed to update that field.
tradeoffs: Agent action catalog vs locked fields
follow_ups: How do you stop the agent updating Amount?
weak_answer_warnings: Tune the prompt until the math settles

interview_questions.question: When is a combination the right choose rather than a single family?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When two outcomes are real: a score the agent may read, a Flow the agent may launch, or a template an invocable may call. Each family still has its own tests.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Help allows templates as invocables and agents that use flows and Apex. I combine when the user journey actually crosses families, not to look modern. I still refuse a mega-agent that also tries to be OWD, validation, and scoring. I write the seams: which field is the contract between predictive and the agent.
interview_questions.example: Predictive LAB_Churn__c; agent FAQ uses it only as context; Flow still sets Status.
follow_ups: How do you test the seam?

interview_questions.question: Give a 30-second choose for a panel that still says Einstein Copilot for everything.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Copilot was renamed to Agentforce. Agentforce is only the conversation-plus-jobs family. Math stays Flow. Scores stay predictive. Drafts stay Prompt Builder. I will not put everything in an agent.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I correct the name, then I run the four questions. I mention grounding, Trust, testing, and human transfer as the cost of choosing an agent so they hear it is not free wow. I mark SKUs Needs verification. I offer to rewrite their slide into four rows before any purchase conversation. That is interview-ready and operable.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard: four boxes, Copilot crossed out, Agentforce only on the chat box.
tradeoffs: Correcting the interviewer vs shared language
follow_ups: What would you build in week one?
weak_answer_warnings: Nodding along with Copilot for everything
